chapter: St. Louis bands and other players
title: Dewey Jackson, Charlie Creath and white versus colored bands on St. Louis boats
summary: Colored bands on the cheaper boat, white bands from Chicago on the deluxe boat, including Jules Buffano and Ralph Williams.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: What about Dewey Jackson? Do you remember him? Yeah, he played on the road.

He played on the St. Paul for years. He's now a porter up to Jeltson, I guess. He might have someone up there. He had been. I think he was working somewhere else. He just plays, he plays now a spot job. Pretty good partner player. He's come aboard, bring a band. He's been a band once in a while after a big Maribona. He's gone one or two seasons. And then, uh, Dewey Jackson came down with a band from St. Louis. But a good corner player himself, but, uh, not such a good organiser. But we had the best color band from St. Louis, and it used to be on the list of St. Louis, called Charlie Clip. He was the best. He was a cornet player, and he had rhythm, and, uh, he would have a very fine band. He would compete with any band in the city. We had Charlie Clip in the summertime. Charlie Clip in the summertime. He had two boys operating in St. Louis in the summertime. Charlie Clip in the summertime. Charlie Clip in the summertime. We'd hire a white band in the summertime. We had, uh, Jules Bufino, who'd come down for the summer months on his DS. It was very deluxe boat. And, uh, he's now playing, you know, with, uh, Jimmy Moratti. And he had a band at that time. And, uh, we had Ralph Williams from Chicago. He had a little bit of a nice band. He's still in New Venice now. In Chicago. So we used to hire a band out of Chicago every summer for, uh, the three months we operated this deluxe boat, uh, newbie white. They had the color band in, uh, cheaper boat. They had the white band on the deluxe boat. How much would it cost to get in the deluxe boat? Well, it, it, it was, uh, McDonald's border up. And, uh, this boat, uh, it was a JS power, however. It was a very pretty boat. And, uh, he's run days during the night. And then we would, uh, we'd serve meals. Very good meals on the boat. And it was really considered the place to go. And she would have this, uh, down a pair. I kind of remember now. He would come down and, uh, play on that particular night just to keep thinking of, uh, high-class man, you know.
